record.paper_title: K3: A New Problem List in Low-Dimensional Topology
record.original_question: For knots K1 and K2 in the 3-sphere, let c(K) denote the crossing number of K, the minimal number of crossings among all diagrams of K. Is crossing number additive under connected sum, so that c(K1 # K2) = c(K1) + c(K2)?

evidence.quote: The crossing number c(K) of a knot K in S^3 is the minimal number of crossings in a diagram for K, the minimum being taken over all possible diagrams of K.
Problem 1.1. Is the crossing number additive under connected sum: c(K1#K2) = c(K1) + c(K2)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let a knot be a smooth embedding of the circle $S^1$ into the 3-sphere $S^3$, considered up to ambient isotopy. A diagram of a knot $K$ is a regular projection to a plane recording over/under information at each double point (crossing). Define the crossing number $c(K)$ of a knot $K \subset S^3$ to be the minimum number of crossings over all diagrams of $K$. For two oriented knots $K_1, K_2 \subset S^3$, let $K_1 \# K_2$ denote their connected sum, formed by removing a small arc from each and gluing the resulting boundaries respecting orientation.

Determine whether the crossing number is additive under connected sum: that is, prove or disprove that
$$ c(K_1 \# K_2) = c(K_1) + c(K_2) $$
holds for every pair of knots $K_1, K_2$ in $S^3$.
artifact.status_search_result: This is a long-standing open problem in knot theory, dating back at least to the early 20th century and listed in standard problem lists (Kirby's list, and now the K3 list). Partial results are known: additivity has been verified for adequate knots (Lickorish–Thistlethwaite), for alternating knots (Kauffman, Murasugi, Thistlethwaite via the Jones polynomial), and for torus knots (Diao). Lower bounds of the form $c(K_1 \# K_2) \ge (c(K_1)+c(K_2))/k$ for various constants $k$ have been established (e.g., Lackenby proved $c(K_1\#\cdots\#K_n) \ge (c(K_1)+\cdots+c(K_n))/152$). The general case remains unsolved as of 2026.

status_evidence.title: The crossing number of composite knots
status_evidence.snippet: Lackenby proves that the crossing number of a connected sum is bounded below by a definite fraction of the sum of the crossing numbers, but the equality (full additivity) remains open in general.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial additivity (up to a multiplicative constant) is known; full additivity is open.

status_evidence.title: K3: A New Problem List in Low-Dimensional Topology
status_evidence.snippet: Problem 1.1 asks whether c(K1#K2)=c(K1)+c(K2), listed as an open problem.
status_evidence.claim: The additivity of crossing number is currently listed as an open problem.
